name: Zhivini Pole
description: The Slavic paradise — a mythical sunlit meadow of eternal spring where righteous souls rest between lives.
mythology: Zhivini Pole (Field of the Living) is a mythical paradise — the Slavic equivalent of Elysium or Eden. It is a sunlit meadow of eternal spring where the souls of the righteous go to rest. The related concept Vyraj (Vyriy) is the warm southern paradise where birds migrate in winter and where souls rest between reincarnations. In the Slavic three-world cosmology (Prav-Nav-Yav), it exists in Prav — the realm of divine order and the righteous dead. It is described as endless green fields, rivers of milk and honey, and eternal warm sunshine, located beyond the World Ocean at the world's edge where the World Tree stands.

Sacred Animals: All birds (who know the path to Vyraj)

festivals: Ancestor veneration days (Rodunitsa) when souls visit from this realm
